sentences.text: In a study of people with diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome and depression, higher levels of the gut bacterium Bacteroides fragilis were associated with increased depression severity scores.
When mice were exposed to this bacterium or its lipid product C1P, they exhibited depression-like signs, reduced levels of the brain enzyme SMPD4, and myelin loss in the hippocampus.
Boosting SMPD4 via viral vectors or limiting branched-chain amino acids in the diet partially reversed these behavioral and myelin changes in the animals.
The authors suggest a pathway where B. fragilis leads to brain myelin damage via C1P, though the mechanism for how this lipid travels from the gut to the brain remains unexplained.
